prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1234; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the left lane of a two-lane road in Houston, Texas, when the vehicle struck the front of a northbound vehicle operated by Driver 2 in a low-speed head-on collision. Upon arrival, the responding officer observed that the front end of Driver 1's vehicle and the front bumper area of Driver 2's vehicle showed damage consistent with the reported impact. Driver 1 was seated in the driver's position and remained at the scene. Driver 1 reported neck strain, and the nature of the collision and the force involved are consistent with that complaint. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general positions of both vehicles and the location of debris, although no independent witnesses were identified who observed the collision itself. Statements from both drivers and a passenger, who was present in the rear seat, were taken and align with the officer's observations regarding the vehicle's occupancy at the time of the crash. Records show no prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle, and Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the applicable policy.
